svg.text: Oncor Longshore–Drill Hole 765 kV — Approved Route
PUCT Docket 59029 · Route 476 · 181.6 miles · 8 Permian Basin counties · Big Spring to Reeves County
MILES BY COUNTY (approximate, along the approved centerline)
WHAT A FIRST OFFER USUALLY LEAVES OUT
What the line does to the value of the land you keep — not just the strip they take.
Where their trucks enter, how often, and what happens to your gates, roads and fences.
Extra ground used during construction, separate from the permanent easement.
Ruts, compaction, terraces, drainage and re-seeding — put in writing before you sign.
The agency has a team. Now you do too.
Owner-side only, nationwide, since the 1980s. We never work for the condemning agency, utility or pipeline.
No upfront cost — contingency only. Our fee is a percentage of the additional compensation we secure;
if we don’t increase your payout, you owe us nothing. Legal counsel coordinated when your case requires it.
National ROW is a right-of-way consulting firm, not a law firm. Nothing here is legal advice.
FREE REVIEW BY A SENIOR CONSULTANT
Text or email a photo of your offer letter — we read it free.
Route geometry from Oncor’s public CCN project mapping service; mileage and county figures computed from that data and cross-checked against Oncor’s published project length.
The line shown is the approved CENTERLINE — the easement is a corridor roughly 200 feet wide centered on it, and the final surveyed alignment can shift within the approved corridor.
This map is an approximation for landowner orientation. It is not a survey, not an appraisal, and not legal advice.
